title: Diagram object classes as morphisms of simplicial homotopy categories
statement:
Use simplicial and combinatorial model categories and projective diagram models as in [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], the Bergner homotopy category $h\mathrm{sCat}=\mathrm{sCat}[W_{\mathrm{DK}}^{-1}]$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property], and chunks as in [lem-coef-simplicial-small-chunks]. For a model category $\mathcal B$, write $\pi_0\mathcal B$ for its objects modulo zigzags of weak equivalences (equivalently, isomorphism classes in its ordinary homotopy category). Let $\mathcal A$ be a combinatorial simplicial model category and $I$ a small simplicial category. Taking a projectively cofibrant fibrant representative of a diagram, and regarding it as a simplicial functor $I\to\mathcal A^{cf}$, induces a bijection
$$\pi_0(\mathcal A^I)\ \cong\ \operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I,\mathcal A^{cf}).$$
It is natural under restriction in $I$ (computed with derived restriction and replacement if necessary). Universes are chosen to contain the displayed target; the test category $I$ remains small in the original universe.

If $I$ is cofibrant and $U$ is an $I$-chunk of $\mathcal A$, the same construction gives a bijection
$$\pi_0(U^I)\ \cong\ \operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I,U^{cf}),$$
where the equivalence relation on $U^I$ is generated by objectwise weak equivalences between diagrams with values in $U$. This restricted bijection commutes with the inclusions into the unrestricted bijection. In particular, for simplicial functors $f,g:I\to U^{cf}$, their homotopy-category classes agree exactly when they are connected by such a zigzag of objectwise weak equivalences.

This states a classification of OBJECT classes, not a coherent diagram-category equivalence. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: First let $I$ be cofibrant and let $U$ be an $I$-chunk (the case $U=\mathcal A$ is allowed). Put $T=U^{cf}$. Its mapping sets are Kan: apply the simplicial model axiom of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] to the initial map of the cofibrant source and the terminal map of the fibrant target. Hence $T$ is Bergner fibrant. The span category of [lem-coef-chunk-span-path-object] supplies a specified factorization $T\xrightarrow{\tau}P(U)\xrightarrow{(\pi_0,\pi_1)}T\times T$ of the diagonal, with $\tau$ a weak equivalence and the second arrow a fibration. The proof below uses exactly this path object, whose middle objects remain in $U$.

source.place: A.3.4 opening paragraph and A.3.4.7-A.3.4.10: fibrant targets and the span path object.

proof.text: Let $f,g:I\to T$ represent the same morphism of $h\mathrm{sCat}$. By [lem-coef-model-localization-homotopy-classes] in the Bergner model category there is a left homotopy $H:J\to T$ with endpoints $f,g$ and weak retraction $c:J\to I$. To get a good cylinder without imposing any extra condition on that lemma, factor the endpoint map $I\amalg I\to J$ as a cofibration $I\amalg I\to J'$ followed by a trivial fibration $t:J'\to J$. Replace $H,c$ by $Ht,ct$. Both new endpoint maps $e_0,e_1:I\to J'$ are cofibrations, since $I$ is cofibrant; they are weak equivalences since $(ct)e_k=1$ and $ct$ is a weak equivalence. Lift the square with left map $e_0$, top map $\tau f:I\to P(U)$, bottom map $(fct,Ht):J'\to T\times T$ and right map $(\pi_0,\pi_1)$. Its lift $L:J'\to P(U)$ exists by the model lifting axiom. Then $h=Le_1$ has endpoints $f,g$. Taking the apex of each span $h(i)$ gives an enriched diagram $a:I\to U$ and enriched natural transformations $f\leftarrow a\to g$ which are objectwise weak equivalences. Thus equality in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ gives a zigzag entirely inside $U^I$.

source.place: Proof of A.3.4.10, (1) implies (2); explicit left-to-right homotopy lifting using the fundamental lemma (also Mathlib Homotopy.lean:43-61).

proof.text: Conversely, let $f,g:I\to T$ be joined by a zigzag of objectwise weak equivalences in $U^I$. It makes them isomorphic in $\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal A^I)$. The empty coproduct factorization in the chunk $U^I$ gives a projective trivial fibration $\alpha:a\to f$ with $a\in U^I$ projectively cofibrant. Since $f$ is objectwise fibrant, so is $a$. The isomorphism $[a]\to[g]$ obtained by composing $[\alpha]$ with the given isomorphism $[f]\to[g]$ has a representative $\beta:a\to g$ by [lem-coef-model-localization-map-surjective] in $\mathcal A^I$. It is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences]. Fullness puts this map in $U^I$. Factor $(\alpha,\beta):a\to f\times g$ using the two-member product factorization in the chunk $U^I$: $a\xrightarrow{u}b\xrightarrow{v}f\times g$, where $u$ is a projective trivial cofibration, $v$ a projective fibration and $b\in U^I$. Both projections of $v$ are weak equivalences by two-out-of-three. The diagram $b$ is projectively cofibrant because $a$ is, and fibrant because $v$ is a fibration with fibrant target. Evaluation therefore makes each $b(i)$ bifibrant, and $v$ defines $h:I\to P(U)$ with endpoints $f,g$. In the Bergner localization, $[\pi_0][\tau]=[\pi_1][\tau]=1$ and $[\tau]$ is invertible, so $[\pi_0]=[\pi_1]$ and $[f]=[g]$.

source.place: Proof of A.3.4.10, (2) implies (1); the representative of the isomorphism and the factorization of the pair are written explicitly.

proof.text: For a diagram $F\in U^I$, empty-family factorizations in the chunk $U^I$ first give a cofibrant replacement $a\to F$ by a projective trivial fibration and then a fibrant replacement $a\to b$ by a projective trivial cofibration. Both replacement objects lie in $U^I$, and $b$ is projectively bifibrant, hence objectwise bifibrant. The diagram $b:I\to T$ defines the proposed map on classes. Different replacements and diagrams in the same weak-equivalence class give the same map by Step 3. If their maps agree, Step 2 joins the representatives inside $U^I$, proving injectivity. Every Bergner homotopy-category map $I\to T$ is represented by an actual enriched functor $f:I\to T$, by [lem-coef-model-localization-map-surjective] in the Bergner model category of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], since $I$ is cofibrant and $T$ is fibrant. Take a projective trivial fibration $a\to f$ with $a$ cofibrant inside $U^I$. The target $f$ is projectively fibrant, so $a$ is projectively bifibrant. Step 3 shows that its map equals $[f]$. This proves the restricted bijection and proves also that every pointwise bifibrant $f$, whether projectively cofibrant or not, is sent to its actual Bergner class.

source.place: A.3.4.10 and proof of A.3.4.12: projective replacements, injectivity, and representation of homotopy-category maps by strict functors.

proof.text: Since $\mathcal A$ is an $I$-chunk of itself, Step 4 with $U=\mathcal A$ gives the unrestricted bijection when $I$ is cofibrant. The same proof, with the same diagrams and span apices, is used before and after including an $I$-chunk $U$ into $\mathcal A$. It follows that the restricted bijection commutes with inclusion: a projectively bifibrant representative chosen in $U^I$ is also such a representative in $\mathcal A^I$, and the represented simplicial functor is literally unchanged.

source.place: A.3.4.12, reduction to cofibrant indices; compatibility of the A.3.4.10 construction with a full chunk inclusion.

proof.text: For a general small $I$, take a small Bergner cofibrant replacement $v:J\to I$. By [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], $v_!\dashv v^*$ is a Quillen equivalence. Restriction preserves all objectwise weak equivalences; its derived functor is therefore ordinary restriction on classes. Its inverse on classes is $[F]\mapsto[v_!QF]$, using a projectively cofibrant replacement $QF$. Independence of the replacement and preservation of weak equivalences follow from the derived-functor statement of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], which says that a left Quillen functor preserves weak equivalences between cofibrant objects. Here are both inverse checks using the stated Quillen-equivalence criterion. For fibrant $G\in\mathcal A^I$, the adjoint of a cofibrant replacement $Qv^*G\to v^*G$ is a weak equivalence $v_!Qv^*G\to G$. For cofibrant $F\in\mathcal A^J$, choose a fibrant replacement $v_!F\to Rv_!F$; its adjoint $F\to v^*Rv_!F$ is a weak equivalence. Replacing general $G,F$ first yields a bijection $v^*:\pi_0(\mathcal A^I)\to\pi_0(\mathcal A^J)$. On the other side, precomposition with $[v]$ is a bijection of Bergner Hom sets, since $v$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence.

source.place: A.3.4.12, first sentence, using A.3.3.8. Derived unit and counit are expanded into the two class-level inverse checks.

proof.text: If $F:I\to\mathcal A^{cf}$ is any pointwise bifibrant diagram, then $v^*F:J\to\mathcal A^{cf}$ is pointwise bifibrant. Step 4 for $U=\mathcal A$ says that its diagram class corresponds to $[Fv]$. Consequently, for any projectively bifibrant representative $F$ of an $I$-diagram class, its Bergner class maps under precomposition with $v$ to the already established class bijection for $J$. Both vertical arrows in Step 6 are bijections. This proves that the construction for $I$ is independent of the representative and bijective. The same argument applied to an arbitrary pointwise bifibrant $F$ shows that its class maps to $[F]$ even when $F$ is not projectively cofibrant: compare it to a projectively bifibrant replacement after restriction to $J$ and then cancel $[v]$.

source.place: A.3.4.12: the change-of-index square, with no assumption that the original index is cofibrant.

proof.text: For a simplicial functor $w:I'\to I$, choose a projectively bifibrant representative $F$ over $I$. The restricted diagram $Fw$ is pointwise bifibrant and represents the derived restriction of the original diagram, because restriction preserves all objectwise weak equivalences. Step 7 identifies its image with $[Fw]=[F][w]$. Thus both routes around the naturality square agree on every class, including when either index is not cofibrant. Step 5 already gives compatibility with chunk inclusions. Finally Steps 2 and 3 give exactly the last asserted equivalence for $f,g:I\to U^{cf}$. Every index replacement and diagram construction uses the original small index universe; only the target model category, span category and displayed hom sets require the larger ambient universe.
